5716.colorWord: green leg, orange toes, grey foot base

shape.description: One T-Rex leg, the plain-sided one in the plan's inset: rounded green thigh with hip buckle, orange ribbed toes, standing on a grey two-arch foot base. Snaps to the M-58 hip. The two legs stand 2 cells apart, with one empty cell between.
shape.sizeBasis: Rough estimate: one cell about 52 mm and one slot about 36 mm, scaled from Joey's hand in IMG_0954 and IMG_0956; no ruler measurement.

accepts: two floor cells in a line
or two blocks of equal height

physics.behaviour: Holds the T-Rex up. No marble touches it. Part of the T-Rex, which stays assembled in every level.

evidence.shows: Dinosaur's legs align with the buckle and snap in

evidence.source: trex_plans_07.png step 1-6 inset, trex_plans_12.png step 2-8 inset, trex_plans_19.png step 3-11 inset
evidence.shows: M-57, M-58, M-59 assemble into one T-Rex
Level 1: feet on the floor at rows E-F, columns 3 and 5
Level 2: feet on one block each at H and I, columns 1 and 3 (B-01, B-02, B-01, B-05)
Level 3: feet on the floor at rows D-E, columns 4 and 6

assumptions: Which leg goes on which side is read from the inset only.
faces uses E=+x, W=-x, S=+y, N=-y, in the piece's own frame. Heights are slots above the floor when the piece stands on the floor or, where stated, above the top of its supports.
openQuestions: Does the leg come off for storage, or stay on after the adult assembly?
